biography.plain_text: Maxwell William Ward was a Canadian aviator and founder of Wardair, which grew from northern charter flying into a major international passenger airline. He expanded its fleet and overseas routes before selling the business to Pacific Western Airlines. His entrepreneurial career followed wartime service as a Royal Canadian Air Force instructor.

long_biography.plain_text:
Wardair founder Max Ward insisted that passengers should receive the service they had bought. When his son Kim arranged a holiday package using other airlines for the outward journey, delays and differing standards prompted complaints. Ward ordered refunds for every passenger on the package, including those who had not complained.

Retirement left more time for making things by hand. At his Edmonton workshop, Ward worked with wood and metal, producing furniture and other pieces. He also returned regularly to his northern fishing camp, where former bush-pilot colleagues, family and employees gathered for reunions.
